title: Manufacturing QA LLM prototype - quant & prompt lab notes
content:
Context:
Quick lab notes from the week-long POC with Acme Fabrication (line bots) — goal is an on-site assistant that can:
  - parse short camera+sensor observations and generate triage steps,
  - summarize incident logs into concise root-cause hypotheses,
  - produce short operator-facing instructions compatible with local SOPs.
Constraints:
  - Most inference must run on an on-prem inference node (single GPU, 24GB) behind VPC.
  - Latency target: 200ms median for short prompts (one-shot triage); 600ms allowed for longer summarization flows.
  - Cost sensitivity: customer prefers smaller model runtime but will accept hybrid cascade with hosted fallback for complex queries.
  - Privacy: no raw camera frames leave the private network; RAG vectors can be synced to private store only.
Prototype scope: model selection + quantization strategy + prompt/pipeline tuning. We focused on classification/triage dialogue and incident summarization flows.

Environment & baseline setup:
  - Hardware: single NVIDIA A5000 (24GB) on VPC, k8s node with GPU-operator. 
  - Serving stack: Redwood Private runtime (local), using continuous-batching disabled for low-latency paths.
  - Candidate models pulled from internal catalog: Llama-2-13B (hf conversion), Mistral-7B, Falcon-7B-instruct, and a trimmed Llama-2-7B variant.
  - Quant tooling: GPTQ pipeline (faster conversion) + double-check with AWQ for 4-bit paths.
  - Tokenizer: sentencepiece with 2048 context; offline tokenization for image-caption fused prompts.

Model candidate notes (quick impressions):
  - Mistral-7B: best latency/quality tradeoff for triage prompts when full precision or 4-bit GPTQ-quantized. Strong instruction-following. Memory footprint after 4-bit ~6.5GB resident.
  - Llama-2-13B: highest quality for long-form summarization, but even 8-bit int8 quantization pushes 24GB; impossible to fit on a single A5000 without offloading. Good candidate for hosted fallback.
  - Llama-2-7B (trim): balanced choice — slightly worse summarization but cheaper. After 4-bit quant, fits ~8-10GB depending on optimizer kernels.
  - Falcon-7B-instruct: good at terse instruction responses, but tokenization quirks caused occasional truncation in our SOP templates.

Quantization experiments (configs tried):
  - Config A: GPTQ 4-bit (per-channel, 32-block) + residual MSE tweak. Fast conversions, stable for Mistral-7B and Llama-2-7B.
  - Config B: AWQ hybrid (4-bit + grouped) — slightly better nLL in offline evals but slower kernels on our runtime.
  - Config C: int8 dynamic (experimental) — allowed Llama-13B to load with offloading but tail latency unpredictable.

Key metrics (median across 300 prompts each; synthetic mix of triage and summarization):
  - Mistral-7B FP16 (no quant): median latency 210ms triage, 520ms summarization; mem 11.1GB
  - Mistral-7B GPTQ-4: median 130ms triage, 370ms summarization; mem 6.6GB
  - Llama-2-7B GPTQ-4: median 170ms triage, 420ms summarization; mem 8.2GB
  - Llama-2-13B int8(offload): median 450ms triage (with offload jitter), 1.2s summarization; mem on device 12.2GB + CPU swap
  - Falcon-7B-instruct GPTQ-4: 150ms triage, 410ms summarization; mem 7.4GB
Quality signals (small eval set, 240 labeled examples):
  - Triage correctness (binary: suggested safe/unsafe action): Mistral-7B FP16 92%, GPTQ-4 89%; Llama-2-7B GPTQ-4 86%; Falcon-7B 87%
  - Summarization ROUGE-L (proxy): Llama-2-13B FP16 0.58; Mistral-7B FP16 0.51; Mistral-7B GPTQ-4 0.48
  - Instruction adherence (Does the response mention exact SOP step IDs when appropriate): Mistral-7B FP16 95%, GPTQ-4 92%

Observations:
  - 4-bit GPTQ on Mistral-7B gives the best operational sweet spot for this hardware: low latency, fits memory, minor drop in summarization quality but still within customer tolerance for triage use-case.
  - Long summarization tasks still favor larger FP16 models; recommend a two-stage pipeline (local small model for immediate triage + hosted Llama-13B for deep summarization) if privacy/latency SLOs allow.
  - Tokenizer and prompt engineering matter: SOP templates with embedded IDs and bulleted steps suffer when prompts get free-form. We saw hallucinated step IDs when the prompt context exceeded 600 tokens. Fixed by: explicit enumerated context + instruction 'do not invent new step IDs'.
  - Kernel support: AWQ variants provided slightly better perplexity on offline evals but our runtime kernels are not optimized yet, causing tail latency spikes. Need to coordinate with runtime team for AWQ kernel adoption.

Prompt & pipeline tuning notes (practical):
  - Short triage prompt (first-call flow): 
    System: "You are an on-site manufacturing assistant. Given sensor caption and last 3 log lines, produce a single prioritized next-step (action) and a severity tag (low/med/high). Do not invent SOP IDs. If uncertain, return 'escalate-to-human'."
    User: "sensor: camera-12 anomaly: misaligned-hinge; temp: 74C; logs: [line-1, line-2, line-3]"
    Post-process: map severity to routing policy (high -> immediate operator screen; med -> mobile push)
  - Summarization prompt (deeper flow): chunk incident log into 512-token windows, run retrieval of matching SOP paragraphs, attach top-3 paragraphs as context, instruct model to: (a) list probable root causes with confidence score, (b) recommend 2 corrective steps mapped to SOP IDs if present.
  - Prefix caching: for repeated calls with same SOP context we cache token prefixes to reduce tokenization cost; observed ~12% median latency improvement on triage flows.
  - Reranking: use a small embedding-based reranker (Mistral-embed-lite) + BLEU-based heuristic for ensuring suggested SOP steps match anchor text. Reranker runs on CPU and adds ~25ms. Worth it for precision-sensitive responses.

Failure modes seen during lab runs:
  - Hallucinated SOP IDs (mitigation: explicit negative instruction + post-process verification against local SOP index).
  - Kernel-induced tail latency for AWQ on some prompt shapes (>1s in p99) — avoid AWQ unless we have kernel fixes.
  - Offload jitter for Llama-13B when memory pressure spikes — leads to timeouts in k8s probe.

Recommended deployment pattern for POC (opinionated):
  - Default local runtime: Mistral-7B GPTQ-4 for triage flows (fits single A5000, meets 200ms median).
  - Cascade: if model returns 'escalate-to-human' or confidence < 0.6, fallback to hosted Llama-2-13B FP16 job (hosted API) for deeper summarization or final incident write-up.
  - Use RAG retrieval for summarization: keep private SOP vector store in same VPC
  - Monitoring: track token-level latency, model-confidence, post-rerank precision, SOP-ID-verification-failures. Create alerts for >2x p90 latency or >5% SOP mismatch.

Open questions / next experiments:
  - Try AWQ + runtime kernel patch (runtime ticket filed) to see if AWQ quality gains can be operationally unlocked.
  - Evaluate a trimmed 10B Llama-variant with int8 offloading on our hardware (could simplify cascade if it fits predictably).
  - Prompt engineering: test explicit examples-of-bad outputs in system prompt to reduce hallucinations (contrastive examples).
  - Longer-term: small distilled model trained on customer incident logs (finetune) vs. zero-shot quantized open model — cost/quality trade-off.

Action items (owner tags):
  - Maya: run 48-hour stability test on Mistral-7B GPTQ-4 with continuous traffic simulation (due 2025-02-08).
  - Ravi: file runtime kernel PR for AWQ and coordinate perf tests (JIRA-ENG-1252).
  - Lina: draft operator UI mapping for severity routing and write up SOP-ID verification spec.
  - Elena: scope hosted fallback SLA and estimate cost for fallback volume >10%

Quick appendix (notes-to-self):
  - Keep conversion artifacts in /mnt/conv (hashed by model+config) and version with conversion runtime id.
  - Benchmarks used: synthetic triage set (300), summarization sample (120), labeled eval (240). Share spreadsheets to product team.

Rough verdict for customer meeting:
  - Upfront recommendation: start POC with Mistral-7B GPTQ-4 on local node for triage. Add hosted Llama-13B fallback for deep summarization. Emphasize SOP verification layer to mitigate hallucinations.

End of notes.
